title: Enterprise onboarding: integration, escalation, health checks & QBR playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s standard enterprise onboarding checklist, integration guidance, escalation paths, common known issues and workarounds, ongoing health checks, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) materials. The document is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), and on-call SREs supporting enterprise customers during the first 90 days and ongoing account health cadence.

Scope:
- New Dedicated and Private deployment customers, plus self-serve Hosted customers moving to enterprise support.
- Covers technical integration, SLA commitments, operational escalation, and QBR agenda templates.

Goal:
- Reduce time-to-production for enterprise customers to < 30 days for standard integrations.
- Ensure clear escalation and ownership to meet SLA targets.
- Provide repeatable QBR and health check processes to identify regressions and cost/latency optimization opportunities.

Owners & Roles:
- Customer Success (owner): Aisha Patel (primary) — overall onboarding project owner.
- Solutions Engineering (technical integration): Marcus Lee — onboarding & integration runbooks.
- Eng SRE / Platform (operational support): Jin Park — on-call escalation and incident coordination.
- Account Executive (commercial): assigned per account.
- Customer Technical Contact: designated by customer.

Key SLAs and Targets:
- Initial response SLA:
  - P1 (production outage): 30 minutes initial response, continuous updates every 30 minutes until mitigation.
  - P2 (degraded experience / elevated latency): 4 hours initial response.
  - P3 (non-urgent / feature request): 48 hours initial response.
- Latency SLOs (Dedicated customers): median inference latency for configured route <= 200ms tail-latency (p95) <= 500ms (per agreed profile).
- Availability target for Dedicated pools: 99.9% monthly uptime (per contract).

Onboarding checklist (90-day playbook) — high level:
1. Pre-kickoff (Documentation & Legal)
   - Verify signed contract, SAML/IAM provisioning, and agreed network topology (VPC peering / VPN).
   - Collect customer model versions, expected RPS, typical sequence lengths, and data residency requirements.
2. Week 0 (Kickoff)
   - Introductions: CS, SE, SRE, Security contact. Confirm key success criteria and timelines.
   - Review architecture options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Decide deployment target.
3. Week 1-2 (Integration + Access)
   - Provision environment: Dedicated pool or Private control plane.
   - Exchange API keys / service accounts and configure KMS/HSM if needed.
   - Run smoke tests: health endpoints, basic generate/embedding calls. Example command:
     curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
   - Validate network routes and firewall rules.
4. Week 2-4 (Performance & Load Testing)
   - Run load test with canonical prompt sets and target RPS. Use load harness (internal tool: se-load-runner).
   - Collect baseline metrics: latency percentiles, token cost, error rates.
   - Tune batching and caching profiles (see Quantization & batching recommendations section).
5. Week 4-8 (Cutover & Hardening)
   - Canary traffic plan: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback windows.
   - Verify monitoring dashboards and alerting (latency, error rate, cost delta).
6. Week 8-12 (Stabilize & QBR preparation)
   - Document operational runbooks, train customer on Console, schedule first QBR.

Integration guide — must-do steps (technical):
- Required network ports: 443 outbound for API; for Private deployments, additional health and metrics ports documented in reference-architectures.
- Authentication: support for API keys and SAML/OIDC. For Private installs, verify KMS key access.
- Sample routing config (YAML):
  routes:
    - name: customer-main
      model: gptx-3.8b-q4
      max_tokens: 1024
      timeout_ms: 8000
      fallback_model: gptx-3.8b-q2
- Recommended validation tests (SE run):
  - Smoke: single token generation, embedding accuracy check.
  - Functional: tooling calling, structured output validation (JSON-schema).
  - Performance: 5-minute sustained target RPS at 95th percentile latency target.

Escalation playbook (production support):
- Level definitions:
  - L1 (CS / SE triage): first responder for customer-impacting but isolated issues (e.g., misconfig, key rotation). Channel: #cs-enterprise.
  - L2 (SRE / Platform engineers): handles runtime, autoscaling, GPU allocation, and networking. Pager duty: redwood-sre-oncall.
  - L3 (Eng Serving Runtime / Model team): for deep root-cause analysis (kernel regressions, model scoring regressions).
- Escalation steps (ordered):
  1. Triage in Slack (#cs-enterprise) and open internal ticket in Jira (project: CS-OPS). Include request id, timestamps, sample payloads, and customer impact.
  2. If P1, page redwood-sre-oncall and inform the CS lead. Set incident bridge (Zoom link).
  3. SRE assesses whether to reroute traffic to fallback model/region and execute mitigation steps.
  4. Post-mitigation: run RCA and produce postmortem if incident meets postmortem threshold (>= 1 hour downtime or customer financial impact).
- Communication templates (use in Slack/email):
  - Status update: "We have identified elevated latency affecting customer X. Mitigation in progress; current workaround: route to fallback model. ETA 30m."

Common issues & workarounds (top 6):
| Symptom | Likely cause | Short-term workaround | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| High tail latency on generation | KV cache thrash or oversized batching | Reduce batch size; enable prefix caching; route to smaller sequence length model | SRE/SE |
| Auth failures after rotation | Missing key propagation to Private control plane | Re-sync keys; restart gateway service; provide temporary API key | CS/SE |
| Elevated token cost suddenly | Model variant fallback to larger model during autoscale | Force route to cost-optimized quantized profile; disable overflow autoscale | SE/Finance |
| 5xx errors from routing-service | OOM on GPU-host or kernel mismatch | Fallback to replica in other region; scale out GPU pool; open kernel mismatch ticket | SRE/Runtime |
| Inconsistent structured output (JSON schema fails) | Model prompt drift or temperature changes | Lock prompt template; pin model version; lower temperature | SE/Customer |
| Embedding quality drop | Model checkpoint mismatch / quantization regression | Roll back model to previous checkpoint; compare eval prompts | SE/Applied-ML |

Operational runbooks (selected):
- High-latency spike (SRE):
  1. Confirm incident severity (p95/p99 increase > 2x baseline).
  2. Check routing-service and GPU host metrics (CPU/GPU utilization, mem, nvlink).
  3. If GPU OOMs: drain node, spin up replacement; route traffic to fallback region/pool.
  4. If KV cache thrash: clear cache for impacted route and increase cache size; document in incident.
  5. Follow up with tuning: adjust batch window and cache TTLs.
- Auth failure after key rotation (SE):
  1. Verify key propagation in control plane: curl controlplane/api/v1/keys
  2. If missing, trigger re-sync job: /bin/reload-keys --account <acct>
  3. Re-issue temporary key to customer and schedule maintenance window for full switch.

Health checks & QBR materials:
- Weekly health report (automated):
  - Metrics: 7d rolling avg latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate by code, token usage and cost-per-1k-tokens, throughput (RPS), model version usage.
  - Alerts: list of triggered alerts (last 7d) with ack status.
  - Capacity: Dedicated pool utilization and headroom.
- Monthly health check (CS-led):
  - Review above metrics, open action items for improvements, and update customer playbook.
- Quarterly Business Review (QBR) template (30–60 minute agenda):
  1. Introductions & Objectives (5m)
  2. Adoption & Usage trends (10m) — tokens, routes, cost trends
  3. Performance & Reliability (10m) — SLO attainment, incidents, mitigations
  4. Optimization Opportunities (10m) — batching, quantization, model recommendations with estimated cost delta
  5. Roadmap & Ask (10m) — upcoming platform features and customer asks
  6. Action items & next steps (5m)
- QBR deliverables:
  - One-page scorecard (SLOs, costs, incidents, adoption KPIs)
  - List of prioritized action items, owners, and target dates

Reporting templates & examples:
- One-page scorecard columns: SLO (metric), Current status, Target, Trend, Owner
- Example KPI snapshot: "Production routes: 4 | 30d tokens: 12.8M | Cost per 1k tokens: $0.42 | p95 latency: 380ms"

Security & compliance checks during onboarding:
- Confirm data residency and retention policy alignment.
- Verify audit logging for all control-plane actions and KMS access.
- For Private installs: run compliance checklist (see /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging).

Escalation communication checklist:
- Always include: request_id, timestamps, sample payloads (with PII redacted), environment, and business impact.
- Use centralized incident ticketing: Jira ticket created within 10 minutes of P1 declaration.

Post-onboarding handoff:
- Finalize runbook and hand to customer success manager for ongoing health checks.
- Schedule first monthly health check and first QBR (within 45 days of production cutover).
